bug_semantics: Ech0 stored local-account passwords as a single unsalted MD5 hex digest. MD5Encrypt(text) is crypto/md5.New, Write([]byte(text)), Sum(nil), hex.EncodeToString — no salt, no iteration, no memory-hard KDF. Through 5.4.1 every local-password path used that helper: InitOwner and Register persist MD5Encrypt(password) into users.password; Login hashes the submitted password the same way and does a string equality check against the stored digest; UpdateUser rewrites users.password with another unsalted MD5. An attacker who obtains data/ech0.db (backup export, mis-served static files, or filesystem access) can extract the 32-hex hashes and recover owner/admin plaintext with rainbow tables or GPU hashcat -m 0, then POST /api/login for a full session JWT. CWE-327. Fixed in 5.4.2 by moving the secret into user_local_auth, hashing new passwords with bcrypt, and lazily upgrading leftover MD5 rows on next successful login.
